She said: 'I do not know. He is here, withdrawn in this upper chamber (mashrabah, meaning the upper room).' So I came to a black servant of his and said: 'Ask permission for 'Umar.' The servant entered, then came out to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I went and came to the pulpit, where there was a group sitting, some of whom were weeping. I sat for a little while, then what I felt overcame me, so I came to the servant and said: 'Ask permission for 'Umar.' He entered, then came out and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I went out and sat by the pulpit, then what I felt overcame me again, so I came to the servant and said: 'Ask permission for 'Umar.' He entered, then came out to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I turned to leave, and the servant called me back and said: 'Enter, he has given you permission.' I entered and greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and found him reclining on a mat of woven reeds (rumal hasir)."

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub also narrated it to us, in the hadith of Salih: "a mat of woven reeds which had left its mark on his side." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, have you divorced your wives?" He raised his head to me and said: "No." I said: "Allahu akbar! If only you had seen us, O Messenger of Allah, when we were a people of Quraysh who dominated women. When we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women dominated them, so our women began to learn from their women. One day I became angry with my wife, and she began to argue back at me. I disapproved that she should argue back at me, and she said: 'Why do you disapprove that I argue back at you? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ argue back at him, and one of them will abandon him until night.' I said: 'Whoever among you does that has failed and lost. Are you safe, that one of you will be subject to Allah's anger because of the anger of His Messenger, and then she will be destroyed?'" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I entered upon Hafsah and said: 'Do not let it deceive you that your neighbour is more beautiful, or more beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you.'" He smiled again. I said: "May I keep you company, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." So I sat down, and I raised my head and looked around the room. By Allah, I saw nothing in the room that caught the eye except three hides (ahbah thalathah). I said: "Ask Allah, O Messenger of Allah, to expand provision for your Ummah, for He has expanded it for Persia and Rome, and they do not worship Allah." He sat up straight and said: "Are you in doubt, O son of al-Khattab? Those are a people whose good things have been hastened to them in the life of this world." I said: "Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah." He had sworn that he would not enter upon them for a month, out of his intense displeasure with them, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, rebuked him.

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, through various routes, from al-Zuhri, with the same content. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated it from the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, from 'Ubayd ibn Hunayn, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I remained for a year wanting to ask 'Umar ibn al-Khattab about a verse, but I could not bring myself to ask him, out of awe of him, until he set out for Hajj and I set out with him. When we returned, and we were on part of the road, he turned aside to the arak (a tree, Salvadora persica) for a need of his. I waited until he had finished, then I walked with him and said: 'O Commander of the Believers, who were the two women who backed each other against the Prophet ﷺ?'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4913; Sahih Muslim, no. 1479.]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Muslim's wording is: "Who are the two women of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you two back each other against him﴾?" He said: "'A'ishah and Hafsah." Then he related the hadith in full, and some narrators abridged it.

Muslim also said: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, 'Umar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi narrated to us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, from Simak ibn al-Walid (Abu Zumayl): 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas narrated to me, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me, who said: "When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ withdrew from his wives, I entered the mosque and found people scratching the ground with pebbles and saying: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has divorced his wives!' That was before the veil was prescribed. I said: 'I will certainly find out about this today...'" He mentioned the hadith regarding his entering upon 'A'ishah and Hafsah and admonishing them, until he said: "I entered, and there was Rabah, the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, at the threshold of the upper room. I called out and said: 'O Rabah, ask permission for me to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ...'" He mentioned something similar to what preceded, until he said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what troubles you of matters concerning women? If you have divorced them, then Allah is with you, and His angels, Jibril and Mika'il, and I, and Abu Bakr, and the believers are with you. I seldom speak, and praise Allah, without hoping that Allah will confirm my words.'" And this verse was revealed, the verse of choice: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾ and ﴿And if you two back each other against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous of the believers, and the angels after that are supporters﴾. I said: "Did you divorce them?" He said: "No." So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: "He has not divorced his wives!" And this verse was revealed: ﴿And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they spread it. But if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those who [can] draw conclusions from it would have known it﴾ [an-Nisa': 83]. So I was the one who drew that conclusion [Sahih Muslim, no. 1479].

Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Dahhak and others, regarding ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾: they are Abu Bakr and 'Umar. al-Hasan al-Basri added: and 'Uthman. Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said, from Mujahid: regarding ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, he said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: A trustworthy man informed me, traced back to 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding His words: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, that it is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Its chain is weak, and it is extremely unusual (munkar).

Al-Bukhari said: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: 'Umar said: "The wives of the Prophet ﷺ gathered together in jealousy over him, so I said to them: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾, and then this verse was revealed" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4916].

It has already been mentioned that he (i.e., 'Umar) agreed with the Qur'an in several places, among them the revelation regarding the veil, and among them the prisoners of Badr, and among them his saying: "Should you not take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, and al-Ansari narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "News reached me of something that had passed between the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet ﷺ, so I went around questioning them (fastaqraytuhunna), saying: 'You must stop, or Allah will surely replace him with wives better than you.' Until I came to the last of the Mothers of the Believers, and she said: 'O Umar! Does the Messenger of Allah not admonish his wives, that you must admonish them?!' So I fell silent. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, submissive, faithful, obedient, penitent, worshipping, travelling, previously married and virgins﴾."

This woman who turned him back from admonishing the wives was Umm Salamah, as is established in Sahih al-Bukhari [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4483. I have not found in it an explicit statement that she was Umm Salamah, and Allah knows best].

Al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Na'ilah al-Asbahani narrated to us, Isma'il al-Bajali narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾. He said: Hafsah entered upon the Prophet ﷺ in her house while he was with Mariyah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Do not tell 'A'ishah until I give you good news: your father will govern the affair after Abu Bakr if I die." So Hafsah went and told 'A'ishah. 'A'ishah said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Who informed you of this?" He said: ﴿The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me﴾. 'A'ishah said: "I will not look at you until you forbid Mariyah," so he forbade her, and Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid...﴾ [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/117). Its weakness: in it is Isma'il al-Bajali, who is weak, and al-Dahhak did not meet Ibn Abbas, so it is disconnected (munqati').]

Its chain is open to question, and what we have cited makes clear the explanation of these noble verses. The meaning of His words ﴿Muslimat, mu'minat, qanitat, ta'ibat, 'abidat﴾ is evident.

* *

As for His words ﴿sa'ihat﴾, it means fasting women (sa'imat). This was said by Abu Hurayrah, 'A'ishah, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Malik, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and others. A marfu' hadith about it has already been mentioned at His words ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾ in Surah al-Bara'ah, and its wording is: "The travelling of this Ummah is fasting."

Zayd ibn Aslam and his son 'Abd al-Rahman said: ﴿sa'ihat﴾ means emigrating women (muhajirat). 'Abd al-Rahman recited: ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾ [al-Tawbah: 112], meaning the emigrants (al-muhajirun). The first opinion is more preferable, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words ﴿thayyibat wa abkara﴾, it means that among them are previously married women and among them are virgins, so that this would be more appealing to souls, for variety refreshes the soul; this is why He said: ﴿thayyibat wa abkara﴾.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Abu Bakr ibn Sadaqah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Umayyah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Quddus narrated to us, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father: ﴿thayyibat wa abkara﴾. He said: Allah promised His Prophet ﷺ in this verse that He would marry him to them; the thayyib is Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh, and the abkar is Maryam daughter of 'Imran [I have not found this in the published Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani].

The hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned, in the biography of "Maryam (peace be upon her)", through the route of Suwayd ibn Sa'id: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from al-Dahhak and Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, who said: Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the news of the death of Khadijah, and said: "Allah sends her His peace, and gives her good news of a house in Paradise of reed, far from any clamour or toil, of a hollow pearl, between the house of Maryam daughter of 'Imran and the house of Asiyah daughter of Muzahim" [Ta'rikh Dimashq (p. 383), "Tarajim al-Nisa'", ed. Majma' al-'Ilmi bi-Dimashq].

And from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that the Prophet ﷺ entered upon Khadijah while she was dying, and said: "O Khadijah, when you meet your co-wives, convey my greetings to them." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, did you marry before me?" He said: "No, but Allah married me to Maryam daughter of 'Imran, Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh, and Kulthum the sister of Musa." Weak also [Ta'rikh Dimashq (p. 384), "Tarajim al-Nisa'", ed. Majma' al-'Ilmi bi-Dimashq].

Abu Ya'la said: Ibrahim ibn 'Ar'arah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Nur ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Yunus ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been informed that Allah married me in Paradise to Maryam daughter of 'Imran, Kulthum the sister of Musa, and Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh." I said: "May it be pleasant for you, O Messenger of Allah" [It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/309) and al-'Uqayli in al-Du'afa' (4/459) through the route of 'Abd al-Nur ibn 'Abd Allah; 'Abd al-Nur is a liar. Al-'Uqayli said: "It is not preserved."].

This also is weak, and it has been narrated as mursal from Ibn Abi Dawud.

**Commentary on Surah At-Tahrim**, which is Medinan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Scholars differed about the occasion of revelation (*sabab al-nuzul*) of the opening of this surah. It was said that it was revealed concerning Mariyah, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had forbidden to himself. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives?﴾ and the rest of the verse.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Ibrahim ibn Yunus ibn Muhammad informed us, my father narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a slave-girl whom he had intercourse with, but 'A'ishah and Hafsah kept at him until he forbade her. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ up to the end of the verse. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11607).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi [[In A: "al-Raqi".]] narrated to me, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Abu Ghassan narrated to us, Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had intercourse with Umm Ibrahim in the house of one of his wives. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, in my house and on my bed?!" So he made her forbidden to himself. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can the lawful become forbidden to you?" So he swore by Allah that he would not have intercourse with her. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ Zayd ibn Aslam said: his saying "You are forbidden to me" is idle talk (laghw). [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/100).]]

Similarly, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd narrated from his father.

Ibn Jarir also said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: "Say to her: 'You are forbidden to me, and by Allah I will not have intercourse with you.'"

Sufyan al-Thawri and Ibn 'Ulayyah said, from Da'ud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took an oath (*ila'*) and forbade [something to himself], so he was rebuked for the prohibition, and he was commanded to pay the expiation (*kaffarah*) for the oath. Ibn Jarir narrated it. It is similarly reported from Qatadah and others, from al-Sha'bi himself. Likewise, many of the early scholars (*salaf*) said, among them al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas the story in a lengthier form.

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn Yahya narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, "Who are the two wives?" He said: "'A'ishah and Hafsah." The beginning of the report concerned Umm Ibrahim the Qibtiyyah, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had intercourse with in Hafsah's house during her turn. Hafsah became displeased and said: "O Prophet of Allah, you have done with me something you have not done with any of your wives, on my day, in my dwelling, and on my bed." He said: "Are you not pleased that I forbid her to myself, so I will not approach her?" She said: "Yes." So he forbade her and said: "Do not mention that to anyone." But she mentioned it to 'A'ishah, so Allah made Him [the Prophet] aware of it, and Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives?﴾ and the verses [[In M and A: "the verses all of them".]]. It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) expiated his oath and had intercourse with his slave-girl. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/102); its origin is in the Sahih and will come.]]

Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb said in his Musnad: Abu Qilabah 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad al-Raqashi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Hafsah: "Do not tell anyone, and Umm Ibrahim is forbidden to me." She said: "Do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?" He said: "By Allah, I will not approach her." He said: So he did not approach her until she informed 'A'ishah. He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths.﴾

This is a sound chain of narration (*isnad sahih*), but none of the authors of the six canonical books (*al-kutub al-sittah*) recorded it. Al-Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi chose it in his book *al-Mustakhraj*. [[Al-Mukhtarah by Diya' al-Maqdisi, no. (189).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, Hisham al-Dastawa'i narrated to us, who said: Yahya wrote to me, narrating from Ya'la ibn Hakim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that Ibn 'Abbas used to say concerning *al-haram* (declaring something forbidden): it is an oath which one expiates. And Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21], meaning that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade his slave-girl, so Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths.﴾ So he expiated his oath, and thus made the forbidding into an oath. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/101).]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Mu'adh ibn Fadalah, from Hisham (that is al-Dastawa'i), from Yahya (that is Ibn Kathir), from Ibn Hakim (that is Ya'la), from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning *al-haram*: "It is an oath which is expiated." And Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4911).]]

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Hisham al-Dastawa'i with the same wording. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1473).]]

Al-Nasa'i said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Ali informed us, Makhlad (that is Ibn Yazid) narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man came to him and said: "I have made my wife forbidden to me?" He said: "You have lied; she is not forbidden to you." Then he recited this verse: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ "The strictest of the expiations is incumbent upon you: freeing a slave."

Al-Nasa'i alone narrated it through this chain, with this wording. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11609).]]

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Muslim, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade his concubine. [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/86).]]

From here, some jurists who held that expiation is obligatory upon one who forbids his slave-girl, his wife, food, drink, clothing, or any other permissible thing, went this way. This is the view of Imam Ahmad and a group of scholars. Al-Shafi'i held that expiation is not obligatory for anything other than the wife and the slave-girl, when one forbids them by their very identity, or when he uses an unrestricted prohibition concerning them in his statement. However, if he intended by the prohibition the divorce of his wife or the freeing of his slave-girl, it takes effect concerning them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Zahrani [[In M: "al-Tabarani".]] informed me, Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani informed us, al-Hakam ibn Aban informed us, 'Ikrimah narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ concerning the woman who gave herself to the Prophet (ﷺ).

This is a strange (*gharib*) view. The correct view is that it concerned his forbidding of honey, as al-Bukhari said regarding this verse:

Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd [[In A: "from 'Abd".]] ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to drink honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh and would remain with her. So I and Hafsah agreed that whichever of us the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon first, she should say to him: "Have you eaten *maghafir*? I smell *maghafir* from you." He said: "No, but I was drinking honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will not return to it. I have sworn an oath, so do not tell anyone about this." ﴿seeking the approval of your wives﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4912).]]

Thus he narrated this hadith here with this wording. In the chapter of "Oaths and Vows" he said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' claimed that he heard 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr say: I heard 'A'ishah claim that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to remain at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh and drink honey there. So I and Hafsah agreed that whichever of us the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon, she should say: "I smell *maghafir* from you. Have you eaten *maghafir*?" The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon one of them and she said that to him. He said: "No, rather I drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will not return to it." Then this was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ up to: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined﴾, addressed to 'A'ishah and Hafsah, and ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾ refers to his saying: "Rather I drank honey." Ibrahim ibn Musa said, from Hisham: "And I will not return to it, and I have sworn, so do not tell anyone about this." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6691).]]

Similarly, he narrated it in the chapter of "Divorce" through this chain, and its wording is close to it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5267).]] Then he said: *al-maghafir* resembles gum; it occurs on the *ramth* (a type of tamarisk-like shrub) and it has sweetness. *Aghfara al-ramth* means when it has appeared on it. Its singular is *maghfur*, and it is also said *maghafir*. Al-Jawhari also said this. He said: *al-maghfur* may also be found on the *'ushr*, *thumam*, *salam*, and *talh*. He said: *al-Rimth*, with a kasrah, is a pasture among the pastures of camels, and it is of the *hamd* (salty plants). He said: *al-'Urfut* is a tree among the *'idah* (thorny trees), which exudes the *maghfur* [from it]. [[Addition from al-Sihah, entry "'rfT", 3/1142.]]

Muslim also narrated this hadith in the chapter of "Divorce" of his Sahih, from Muhammad ibn Hatim, from Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jurayj, who informed me, 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, with it, and its wording is as al-Bukhari reported it in "Oaths and Vows." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1474).]]

Then al-Bukhari said in the chapter of "Divorce": Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra' narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Mushhir narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) loved sweets and honey, and when he finished the 'Asr prayer he would enter upon his wives, and approach one of them. He entered upon Hafsah bint 'Umar and remained longer than he usually did. So I became jealous and asked about that, and I was told: "A woman from her people gave her a jar of honey, and she gave the Prophet (ﷺ) a drink of it." I said: "By Allah, we will certainly devise a plan against him." So I said to Sawdah bint Zam'ah: "He will approach you. When he comes near you, say: 'Have you eaten *maghafir*?' He will say: 'No.' Then say to him: 'What is this smell I find?' He will say to you: 'Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.' Then say: 'Its bees must have grazed on the *'urfut*.' I will say that, and you, O Safiyyah, say that too." Sawdah said: "By Allah, he had only just stood at the door when I wanted to call out to him with what you had ordered me, out of fear of you. When he came near to her, Sawdah said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, have you eaten *maghafir*?' He said: 'No.' She said: 'Then what is this smell I find from you?' He said: 'Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.' She said: 'Its bees must have grazed on the *'urfut*.' When he came round to me, I said something similar, and when he came round to Safiyyah, she said the same to him. When he came round to Hafsah, she said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall I not give you some of it to drink?' He said: 'I have no need of it.' Sawdah said: 'By Allah, we had deprived him of it.' I said to her: 'Be quiet.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5268).]]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Muslim also narrated it from Suwayd ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn Mushir, with the same wording. He also narrated it from Abu Kurayb, Harun ibn 'Abdullah and al-Hasan ibn Bishr, all three from Abu Usamah Hammad ibn Usamah, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, with the same wording [Sahih Muslim, no. 1474]. In his version, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that a bad smell be detected on him, meaning the foul odour. So they said to him: "You have eaten maghafir (a gum-resin with a strong smell)." When he said: "Rather, I drank honey," they said: "His bees have grazed on the 'urfut (a bitter shrub)," meaning his bees grazed on the 'urfut tree, whose gum is maghafir; so its smell appeared in the honey you drank.

Al-Jawhari said: "Jarasat nahluhu al-'urfut" means that his bees ate it. From this comes the expression for bees: jawaris. The poet said:

"They hover over the thamra'; from them are the jawaris..."

He also said: al-jars and al-jirs mean a faint sound. It is said: "I heard the jars of the bird," when you hear the sound of its beaks on something it is eating. In a hadith: "They will hear the jars of the birds of Paradise." Al-Asma'i said: I was in the gathering of Shu'bah, who said: "fa-yasma'una jarsh tayr al-jannah" with the shin (ش) [marked with a dot]. I said: "Jars?!" He looked at me and said: "Take it from him, for he knows this better than we do" [al-Sihah of al-Jawhari 2/908 and Lisan al-'Arab of Ibn Manzur, root j-r-s].

The point is that this narration states that Hafsah was the one who gave the honey to drink. It comes through the chain of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from his maternal aunt, from 'A'ishah. In another chain, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, it is narrated that Zaynab bint Jahsh was the one who gave the honey to drink, and that 'A'ishah and Hafsah colluded and backed each other against him. Allah knows best. It may be said that these are two separate incidents, and there is no improbability in that; however, whether they were the cause of the revelation of this verse is open to question, and Allah knows best.

Among what indicates that 'A'ishah and Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with them, are the two women who backed each other is the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, where he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Thawr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I was always eager to ask 'Umar about the two wives of the Prophet ﷺ of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined﴾, until 'Umar performed Hajj and I performed Hajj with him. When we were on part of the road, 'Umar turned aside and I turned aside with him carrying the water-vessel. He relieved himself, then came back to me, and I poured water over his hands and he performed ablution. I said: 'O Commander of the Believers, who are the two women of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined﴾?' 'Umar said: 'How astonishing you are, O son of 'Abbas!'" (al-Zuhri said: he disliked it.) "By Allah, I did not ask him about it without him concealing it from me. He said: 'They are Hafsah and 'A'ishah.'" He then began to relate the hadith: "We, the people of Quraysh, were a people who dominated women. When we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women dominated them, so our women began to learn from their women." He said: "My house was in the dwelling of Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd in al-'Awali." He said: "One day I became angry with my wife, and she began to argue back at me. I disapproved that she should argue back at me, and she said: 'Why do you disapprove that I argue back at you? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ argue back at him, and one of them will abandon him until night.'" He said: "So I went and entered upon Hafsah and said: 'Do you argue back at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' She said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And does one of you abandon him until night?' She said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then whoever among you does that has failed and lost. Are you safe, that one of you will be subject to Allah's anger because of the anger of His Messenger, and then she will be destroyed? Do not argue back at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and do not ask him for anything, and ask me for whatever you wish from my wealth. Do not let it deceive you that your neighbour is more beautiful and more beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you'," meaning 'A'ishah. He said: "I had a neighbour from the Ansar, and we took turns going down to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he would go down one day and I would go down one day. He would bring me news of the revelation and other things, and I would bring him the same. We used to hear that Ghassan were shoeing their horses to attack us. My companion went down one day, then came back at night, struck my door and called out to me. I came out to him, and he said: 'A great matter has occurred!' I said: 'What is it? Has Ghassan come?' He said: 'No, something greater and more far-reaching! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has divorced his wives!' I said: 'Hafsah has indeed failed and lost. I had been expecting this to happen.'" He said: "When I had prayed the dawn prayer, I put on my clothes and went down. I entered upon Hafsah, and she was weeping. I said: 'Has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced you?' She said: 'I do not know. He is here, withdrawn in this upper chamber (mashrabah, meaning the upper room).' So I came to a black servant of his and said: 'Ask permission for 'Umar.' The servant entered, then came out to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I went and came to the pulpit, where there was a group sitting, some of whom were weeping. I sat for a little while, then what I felt overcame me, so I came to the servant and said: 'Ask permission for 'Umar.' He entered, then came out and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I went out and sat by the pulpit, then what I felt overcame me again, so I came to the servant and said: 'Ask permission for 'Umar.' He entered, then came out to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I turned to leave, and the servant called me back and said: 'Enter, he has given you permission.' I entered and greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and found him reclining on a mat of woven reeds (rumal hasir)."

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub also narrated it to us, in the hadith of Salih: "a mat of woven reeds which had left its mark on his side." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, have you divorced your wives?" He raised his head to me and said: "No." I said: "Allahu akbar! If only you had seen us, O Messenger of Allah, when we were a people of Quraysh who dominated women. When we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women dominated them, so our women began to learn from their women. One day I became angry with my wife, and she began to argue back at me. I disapproved that she should argue back at me, and she said: 'Why do you disapprove that I argue back at you? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ argue back at him, and one of them will abandon him until night.' I said: 'Whoever among you does that has failed and lost. Are you safe, that one of you will be subject to Allah's anger because of the anger of His Messenger, and then she will be destroyed?'" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I entered upon Hafsah and said: 'Do not let it deceive you that your neighbour is more beautiful, or more beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you.'" He smiled again. I said: "May I keep you company, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." So I sat down, and I raised my head and looked around the room. By Allah, I saw nothing in the room that caught the eye except three hides (ahbah thalathah). I said: "Ask Allah, O Messenger of Allah, to expand provision for your Ummah, for He has expanded it for Persia and Rome, and they do not worship Allah." He sat up straight and said: "Are you in doubt, O son of al-Khattab? Those are a people whose good things have been hastened to them in the life of this world." I said: "Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah." He had sworn that he would not enter upon them for a month, out of his intense displeasure with them, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, rebuked him.

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, through various routes, from al-Zuhri, with the same content. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated it from the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, from 'Ubayd ibn Hunayn, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I remained for a year wanting to ask 'Umar ibn al-Khattab about a verse, but I could not bring myself to ask him, out of awe of him, until he set out for Hajj and I set out with him. When we returned, and we were on part of the road, he turned aside to the arak (a tree, Salvadora persica) for a need of his. I waited until he had finished, then I walked with him and said: 'O Commander of the Believers, who were the two women who backed each other against the Prophet ﷺ?'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4913; Sahih Muslim, no. 1479.]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Muslim's wording is: "Who are the two women of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you two back each other against him﴾?" He said: "'A'ishah and Hafsah." Then he related the hadith in full, and some narrators abridged it.

Muslim also said: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, 'Umar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi narrated to us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, from Simak ibn al-Walid (Abu Zumayl): 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas narrated to me, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me, who said: "When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ withdrew from his wives, I entered the mosque and found people scratching the ground with pebbles and saying: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has divorced his wives!' That was before the veil was prescribed. I said: 'I will certainly find out about this today...'" He mentioned the hadith regarding his entering upon 'A'ishah and Hafsah and admonishing them, until he said: "I entered, and there was Rabah, the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, at the threshold of the upper room. I called out and said: 'O Rabah, ask permission for me to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ...'" He mentioned something similar to what preceded, until he said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what troubles you of matters concerning women? If you have divorced them, then Allah is with you, and His angels, Jibril and Mika'il, and I, and Abu Bakr, and the believers are with you. I seldom speak, and praise Allah, without hoping that Allah will confirm my words.'" And this verse was revealed, the verse of choice: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾ and ﴿And if you two back each other against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous of the believers, and the angels after that are supporters﴾. I said: "Did you divorce them?" He said: "No." So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: "He has not divorced his wives!" And this verse was revealed: ﴿And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they spread it. But if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those who [can] draw conclusions from it would have known it﴾ [an-Nisa': 83]. So I was the one who drew that conclusion [Sahih Muslim, no. 1479].

Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Dahhak and others, regarding ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾: they are Abu Bakr and 'Umar. al-Hasan al-Basri added: and 'Uthman. Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said, from Mujahid: regarding ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, he said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: A trustworthy man informed me, traced back to 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding His words: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, that it is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Its chain is weak, and it is extremely unusual (munkar).

Al-Bukhari said: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: 'Umar said: "The wives of the Prophet ﷺ gathered together in jealousy over him, so I said to them: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾, and then this verse was revealed" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4916].

It has already been mentioned that he (i.e., 'Umar) agreed with the Qur'an in several places, among them the revelation regarding the veil, and among them the prisoners of Badr, and among them his saying: "Should you not take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, and al-Ansari narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "News reached me of something that had passed between the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet ﷺ, so I went around questioning them (fastaqraytuhunna), saying: 'You must stop, or Allah will surely replace him with wives better than you.' Until I came to the last of the Mothers of the Believers, and she said: 'O Umar! Does the Messenger of Allah not admonish his wives, that you must admonish them?!' So I fell silent. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, submissive, faithful, obedient, penitent, worshipping, travelling, previously married and virgins﴾."

This woman who turned him back from admonishing the wives was Umm Salamah, as is established in Sahih al-Bukhari [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4483. I have not found in it an explicit statement that she was Umm Salamah, and Allah knows best].

Al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Na'ilah al-Asbahani narrated to us, Isma'il al-Bajali narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾. He said: Hafsah entered upon the Prophet ﷺ in her house while he was with Mariyah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Do not tell 'A'ishah until I give you good news: your father will govern the affair after Abu Bakr if I die." So Hafsah went and told 'A'ishah. 'A'ishah said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Who informed you of this?" He said: ﴿The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me﴾. 'A'ishah said: "I will not look at you until you forbid Mariyah," so he forbade her, and Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid...﴾ [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/117). Its weakness: in it is Isma'il al-Bajali, who is weak, and al-Dahhak did not meet Ibn Abbas, so it is disconnected (munqati').]

Its chain is open to question, and what we have cited makes clear the explanation of these noble verses. The meaning of His words ﴿Muslimat, mu'minat, qanitat, ta'ibat, 'abidat﴾ is evident.

* *

As for His words ﴿sa'ihat﴾, it means fasting women (sa'imat). This was said by Abu Hurayrah, 'A'ishah, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Malik, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and others. A marfu' hadith about it has already been mentioned at His words ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾ in Surah al-Bara'ah, and its wording is: "The travelling of this Ummah is fasting."

Zayd ibn Aslam and his son 'Abd al-Rahman said: ﴿sa'ihat﴾ means emigrating women (muhajirat). 'Abd al-Rahman recited: ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾ [al-Tawbah: 112], meaning the emigrants (al-muhajirun). The first opinion is more preferable, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words ﴿thayyibat wa abkara﴾, it means that among them are previously married women and among them are virgins, so that this would be more appealing to souls, for variety refreshes the soul; this is why He said: ﴿thayyibat wa abkara﴾.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Abu Bakr ibn Sadaqah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Umayyah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Quddus narrated to us, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father: ﴿thayyibat wa abkara﴾. He said: Allah promised His Prophet ﷺ in this verse that He would marry him to them; the thayyib is Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh, and the abkar is Maryam daughter of 'Imran [I have not found this in the published Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani].

The hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned, in the biography of "Maryam (peace be upon her)", through the route of Suwayd ibn Sa'id: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from al-Dahhak and Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, who said: Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the news of the death of Khadijah, and said: "Allah sends her His peace, and gives her good news of a house in Paradise of reed, far from any clamour or toil, of a hollow pearl, between the house of Maryam daughter of 'Imran and the house of Asiyah daughter of Muzahim" [Ta'rikh Dimashq (p. 383), "Tarajim al-Nisa'", ed. Majma' al-'Ilmi bi-Dimashq].

And from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that the Prophet ﷺ entered upon Khadijah while she was dying, and said: "O Khadijah, when you meet your co-wives, convey my greetings to them." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, did you marry before me?" He said: "No, but Allah married me to Maryam daughter of 'Imran, Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh, and Kulthum the sister of Musa." Weak also [Ta'rikh Dimashq (p. 384), "Tarajim al-Nisa'", ed. Majma' al-'Ilmi bi-Dimashq].

Abu Ya'la said: Ibrahim ibn 'Ar'arah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Nur ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Yunus ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been informed that Allah married me in Paradise to Maryam daughter of 'Imran, Kulthum the sister of Musa, and Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh." I said: "May it be pleasant for you, O Messenger of Allah" [It was also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/309) and al-'Uqayli in al-Du'afa' (4/459) through the route of 'Abd al-Nur ibn 'Abd Allah; 'Abd al-Nur is a liar. Al-'Uqayli said: "It is not preserved."].

This also is weak, and it has been narrated as mursal from Ibn Abi Dawud.

**Commentary on Surah At-Tahrim**, which is Medinan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Scholars differed about the occasion of revelation (*sabab al-nuzul*) of the opening of this surah. It was said that it was revealed concerning Mariyah, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had forbidden to himself. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives?﴾ and the rest of the verse.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Ibrahim ibn Yunus ibn Muhammad informed us, my father narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a slave-girl whom he had intercourse with, but 'A'ishah and Hafsah kept at him until he forbade her. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ up to the end of the verse. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11607).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi [[In A: "al-Raqi".]] narrated to me, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Abu Ghassan narrated to us, Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had intercourse with Umm Ibrahim in the house of one of his wives. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, in my house and on my bed?!" So he made her forbidden to himself. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can the lawful become forbidden to you?" So he swore by Allah that he would not have intercourse with her. Then Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ Zayd ibn Aslam said: his saying "You are forbidden to me" is idle talk (laghw). [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/100).]]

Similarly, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd narrated from his father.

Ibn Jarir also said: Yunus narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: "Say to her: 'You are forbidden to me, and by Allah I will not have intercourse with you.'"

Sufyan al-Thawri and Ibn 'Ulayyah said, from Da'ud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took an oath (*ila'*) and forbade [something to himself], so he was rebuked for the prohibition, and he was commanded to pay the expiation (*kaffarah*) for the oath. Ibn Jarir narrated it. It is similarly reported from Qatadah and others, from al-Sha'bi himself. Likewise, many of the early scholars (*salaf*) said, among them al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas the story in a lengthier form.

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn Yahya narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, "Who are the two wives?" He said: "'A'ishah and Hafsah." The beginning of the report concerned Umm Ibrahim the Qibtiyyah, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had intercourse with in Hafsah's house during her turn. Hafsah became displeased and said: "O Prophet of Allah, you have done with me something you have not done with any of your wives, on my day, in my dwelling, and on my bed." He said: "Are you not pleased that I forbid her to myself, so I will not approach her?" She said: "Yes." So he forbade her and said: "Do not mention that to anyone." But she mentioned it to 'A'ishah, so Allah made Him [the Prophet] aware of it, and Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives?﴾ and the verses [[In M and A: "the verses all of them".]]. It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) expiated his oath and had intercourse with his slave-girl. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/102); its origin is in the Sahih and will come.]]

Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb said in his Musnad: Abu Qilabah 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad al-Raqashi narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Hafsah: "Do not tell anyone, and Umm Ibrahim is forbidden to me." She said: "Do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?" He said: "By Allah, I will not approach her." He said: So he did not approach her until she informed 'A'ishah. He said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths.﴾

This is a sound chain of narration (*isnad sahih*), but none of the authors of the six canonical books (*al-kutub al-sittah*) recorded it. Al-Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi chose it in his book *al-Mustakhraj*. [[Al-Mukhtarah by Diya' al-Maqdisi, no. (189).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, Hisham al-Dastawa'i narrated to us, who said: Yahya wrote to me, narrating from Ya'la ibn Hakim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that Ibn 'Abbas used to say concerning *al-haram* (declaring something forbidden): it is an oath which one expiates. And Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21], meaning that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade his slave-girl, so Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths.﴾ So he expiated his oath, and thus made the forbidding into an oath. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/101).]]

Al-Bukhari narrated it from Mu'adh ibn Fadalah, from Hisham (that is al-Dastawa'i), from Yahya (that is Ibn Kathir), from Ibn Hakim (that is Ya'la), from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning *al-haram*: "It is an oath which is expiated." And Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4911).]]

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Hisham al-Dastawa'i with the same wording. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1473).]]

Al-Nasa'i said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Ali informed us, Makhlad (that is Ibn Yazid) narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man came to him and said: "I have made my wife forbidden to me?" He said: "You have lied; she is not forbidden to you." Then he recited this verse: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ "The strictest of the expiations is incumbent upon you: freeing a slave."

Al-Nasa'i alone narrated it through this chain, with this wording. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11609).]]

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Muslim, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade his concubine. [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/86).]]

From here, some jurists who held that expiation is obligatory upon one who forbids his slave-girl, his wife, food, drink, clothing, or any other permissible thing, went this way. This is the view of Imam Ahmad and a group of scholars. Al-Shafi'i held that expiation is not obligatory for anything other than the wife and the slave-girl, when one forbids them by their very identity, or when he uses an unrestricted prohibition concerning them in his statement. However, if he intended by the prohibition the divorce of his wife or the freeing of his slave-girl, it takes effect concerning them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Zahrani [[In M: "al-Tabarani".]] informed me, Hafs ibn 'Umar al-'Adani informed us, al-Hakam ibn Aban informed us, 'Ikrimah narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ concerning the woman who gave herself to the Prophet (ﷺ).

This is a strange (*gharib*) view. The correct view is that it concerned his forbidding of honey, as al-Bukhari said regarding this verse:

Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd [[In A: "from 'Abd".]] ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to drink honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh and would remain with her. So I and Hafsah agreed that whichever of us the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon first, she should say to him: "Have you eaten *maghafir*? I smell *maghafir* from you." He said: "No, but I was drinking honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will not return to it. I have sworn an oath, so do not tell anyone about this." ﴿seeking the approval of your wives﴾. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4912).]]

Thus he narrated this hadith here with this wording. In the chapter of "Oaths and Vows" he said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' claimed that he heard 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr say: I heard 'A'ishah claim that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to remain at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh and drink honey there. So I and Hafsah agreed that whichever of us the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon, she should say: "I smell *maghafir* from you. Have you eaten *maghafir*?" The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon one of them and she said that to him. He said: "No, rather I drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will not return to it." Then this was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ up to: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined﴾, addressed to 'A'ishah and Hafsah, and ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾ refers to his saying: "Rather I drank honey." Ibrahim ibn Musa said, from Hisham: "And I will not return to it, and I have sworn, so do not tell anyone about this." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6691).]]

Similarly, he narrated it in the chapter of "Divorce" through this chain, and its wording is close to it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5267).]] Then he said: *al-maghafir* resembles gum; it occurs on the *ramth* (a type of tamarisk-like shrub) and it has sweetness. *Aghfara al-ramth* means when it has appeared on it. Its singular is *maghfur*, and it is also said *maghafir*. Al-Jawhari also said this. He said: *al-maghfur* may also be found on the *'ushr*, *thumam*, *salam*, and *talh*. He said: *al-Rimth*, with a kasrah, is a pasture among the pastures of camels, and it is of the *hamd* (salty plants). He said: *al-'Urfut* is a tree among the *'idah* (thorny trees), which exudes the *maghfur* [from it]. [[Addition from al-Sihah, entry "'rfT", 3/1142.]]

Muslim also narrated this hadith in the chapter of "Divorce" of his Sahih, from Muhammad ibn Hatim, from Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jurayj, who informed me, 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, with it, and its wording is as al-Bukhari reported it in "Oaths and Vows." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1474).]]

Then al-Bukhari said in the chapter of "Divorce": Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra' narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Mushhir narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) loved sweets and honey, and when he finished the 'Asr prayer he would enter upon his wives, and approach one of them. He entered upon Hafsah bint 'Umar and remained longer than he usually did. So I became jealous and asked about that, and I was told: "A woman from her people gave her a jar of honey, and she gave the Prophet (ﷺ) a drink of it." I said: "By Allah, we will certainly devise a plan against him." So I said to Sawdah bint Zam'ah: "He will approach you. When he comes near you, say: 'Have you eaten *maghafir*?' He will say: 'No.' Then say to him: 'What is this smell I find?' He will say to you: 'Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.' Then say: 'Its bees must have grazed on the *'urfut*.' I will say that, and you, O Safiyyah, say that too." Sawdah said: "By Allah, he had only just stood at the door when I wanted to call out to him with what you had ordered me, out of fear of you. When he came near to her, Sawdah said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, have you eaten *maghafir*?' He said: 'No.' She said: 'Then what is this smell I find from you?' He said: 'Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.' She said: 'Its bees must have grazed on the *'urfut*.' When he came round to me, I said something similar, and when he came round to Safiyyah, she said the same to him. When he came round to Hafsah, she said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall I not give you some of it to drink?' He said: 'I have no need of it.' Sawdah said: 'By Allah, we had deprived him of it.' I said to her: 'Be quiet.'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5268).]]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Muslim also narrated it from Suwayd ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn Mushir, with the same wording. He also narrated it from Abu Kurayb, Harun ibn 'Abdullah and al-Hasan ibn Bishr, all three from Abu Usamah Hammad ibn Usamah, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, with the same wording [Sahih Muslim, no. 1474]. In his version, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that a bad smell be detected on him, meaning the foul odour. So they said to him: "You have eaten maghafir (a gum-resin with a strong smell)." When he said: "Rather, I drank honey," they said: "His bees have grazed on the 'urfut (a bitter shrub)," meaning his bees grazed on the 'urfut tree, whose gum is maghafir; so its smell appeared in the honey you drank.

Al-Jawhari said: "Jarasat nahluhu al-'urfut" means that his bees ate it. From this comes the expression for bees: jawaris. The poet said:

"They hover over the thamra'; from them are the jawaris..."

He also said: al-jars and al-jirs mean a faint sound. It is said: "I heard the jars of the bird," when you hear the sound of its beaks on something it is eating. In a hadith: "They will hear the jars of the birds of Paradise." Al-Asma'i said: I was in the gathering of Shu'bah, who said: "fa-yasma'una jarsh tayr al-jannah" with the shin (ش) [marked with a dot]. I said: "Jars?!" He looked at me and said: "Take it from him, for he knows this better than we do" [al-Sihah of al-Jawhari 2/908 and Lisan al-'Arab of Ibn Manzur, root j-r-s].

The point is that this narration states that Hafsah was the one who gave the honey to drink. It comes through the chain of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from his maternal aunt, from 'A'ishah. In another chain, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, it is narrated that Zaynab bint Jahsh was the one who gave the honey to drink, and that 'A'ishah and Hafsah colluded and backed each other against him. Allah knows best. It may be said that these are two separate incidents, and there is no improbability in that; however, whether they were the cause of the revelation of this verse is open to question, and Allah knows best.

Among what indicates that 'A'ishah and Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with them, are the two women who backed each other is the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, where he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Thawr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I was always eager to ask 'Umar about the two wives of the Prophet ﷺ of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined﴾, until 'Umar performed Hajj and I performed Hajj with him. When we were on part of the road, 'Umar turned aside and I turned aside with him carrying the water-vessel. He relieved himself, then came back to me, and I poured water over his hands and he performed ablution. I said: 'O Commander of the Believers, who are the two women of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined﴾?' 'Umar said: 'How astonishing you are, O son of 'Abbas!'" (al-Zuhri said: he disliked it.) "By Allah, I did not ask him about it without him concealing it from me. He said: 'They are Hafsah and 'A'ishah.'" He then began to relate the hadith: "We, the people of Quraysh, were a people who dominated women. When we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women dominated them, so our women began to learn from their women." He said: "My house was in the dwelling of Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd in al-'Awali." He said: "One day I became angry with my wife, and she began to argue back at me. I disapproved that she should argue back at me, and she said: 'Why do you disapprove that I argue back at you? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ argue back at him, and one of them will abandon him until night.'" He said: "So I went and entered upon Hafsah and said: 'Do you argue back at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' She said: 'Yes.' I said: 'And does one of you abandon him until night?' She said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then whoever among you does that has failed and lost. Are you safe, that one of you will be subject to Allah's anger because of the anger of His Messenger, and then she will be destroyed? Do not argue back at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and do not ask him for anything, and ask me for whatever you wish from my wealth. Do not let it deceive you that your neighbour is more beautiful and more beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you'," meaning 'A'ishah. He said: "I had a neighbour from the Ansar, and we took turns going down to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he would go down one day and I would go down one day. He would bring me news of the revelation and other things, and I would bring him the same. We used to hear that Ghassan were shoeing their horses to attack us. My companion went down one day, then came back at night, struck my door and called out to me. I came out to him, and he said: 'A great matter has occurred!' I said: 'What is it? Has Ghassan come?' He said: 'No, something greater and more far-reaching! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has divorced his wives!' I said: 'Hafsah has indeed failed and lost. I had been expecting this to happen.'" He said: "When I had prayed the dawn prayer, I put on my clothes and went down. I entered upon Hafsah, and she was weeping. I said: 'Has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced you?' She said: 'I do not know. He is here, withdrawn in this upper chamber (mashrabah, meaning the upper room).' So I came to a black servant of his and said: 'Ask permission for 'Umar.' The servant entered, then came out to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I went and came to the pulpit, where there was a group sitting, some of whom were weeping. I sat for a little while, then what I felt overcame me, so I came to the servant and said: 'Ask permission for 'Umar.' He entered, then came out and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I went out and sat by the pulpit, then what I felt overcame me again, so I came to the servant and said: 'Ask permission for 'Umar.' He entered, then came out to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I turned to leave, and the servant called me back and said: 'Enter, he has given you permission.' I entered and greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and found him reclining on a mat of woven reeds (rumal hasir)."

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub also narrated it to us, in the hadith of Salih: "a mat of woven reeds which had left its mark on his side." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, have you divorced your wives?" He raised his head to me and said: "No." I said: "Allahu akbar! If only you had seen us, O Messenger of Allah, when we were a people of Quraysh who dominated women. When we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women dominated them, so our women began to learn from their women. One day I became angry with my wife, and she began to argue back at me. I disapproved that she should argue back at me, and she said: 'Why do you disapprove that I argue back at you? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ argue back at him, and one of them will abandon him until night.' I said: 'Whoever among you does that has failed and lost. Are you safe, that one of you will be subject to Allah's anger because of the anger of His Messenger, and then she will be destroyed?'" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I entered upon Hafsah and said: 'Do not let it deceive you that your neighbour is more beautiful, or more beloved to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you.'" He smiled again. I said: "May I keep you company, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." So I sat down, and I raised my head and looked around the room. By Allah, I saw nothing in the room that caught the eye except three hides (ahbah thalathah). I said: "Ask Allah, O Messenger of Allah, to expand provision for your Ummah, for He has expanded it for Persia and Rome, and they do not worship Allah." He sat up straight and said: "Are you in doubt, O son of al-Khattab? Those are a people whose good things have been hastened to them in the life of this world." I said: "Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah." He had sworn that he would not enter upon them for a month, out of his intense displeasure with them, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, rebuked him.

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, through various routes, from al-Zuhri, with the same content. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated it from the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, from 'Ubayd ibn Hunayn, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I remained for a year wanting to ask 'Umar ibn al-Khattab about a verse, but I could not bring myself to ask him, out of awe of him, until he set out for Hajj and I set out with him. When we returned, and we were on part of the road, he turned aside to the arak (a tree, Salvadora persica) for a need of his. I waited until he had finished, then I walked with him and said: 'O Commander of the Believers, who were the two women who backed each other against the Prophet ﷺ?'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4913; Sahih Muslim, no. 1479.]

This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Muslim's wording is: "Who are the two women of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you two back each other against him﴾?" He said: "'A'ishah and Hafsah." Then he related the hadith in full, and some narrators abridged it.

Muslim also said: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, 'Umar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi narrated to us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, from Simak ibn al-Walid (Abu Zumayl): 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas narrated to me, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me, who said: "When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ withdrew from his wives, I entered the mosque and found people scratching the ground with pebbles and saying: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has divorced his wives!' That was before the veil was prescribed. I said: 'I will certainly find out about this today...'" He mentioned the hadith regarding his entering upon 'A'ishah and Hafsah and admonishing them, until he said: "I entered, and there was Rabah, the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, at the threshold of the upper room. I called out and said: 'O Rabah, ask permission for me to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ...'" He mentioned something similar to what preceded, until he said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what troubles you of matters concerning women? If you have divorced them, then Allah is with you, and His angels, Jibril and Mika'il, and I, and Abu Bakr, and the believers are with you. I seldom speak, and praise Allah, without hoping that Allah will confirm my words.'" And this verse was revealed, the verse of choice: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾ and ﴿And if you two back each other against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous of the believers, and the angels after that are supporters﴾. I said: "Did you divorce them?" He said: "No." So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: "He has not divorced his wives!" And this verse was revealed: ﴿And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they spread it. But if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those who [can] draw conclusions from it would have known it﴾ [an-Nisa': 83]. So I was the one who drew that conclusion [Sahih Muslim, no. 1479].

Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Dahhak and others, regarding ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾: they are Abu Bakr and 'Umar. al-Hasan al-Basri added: and 'Uthman. Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said, from Mujahid: regarding ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, he said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: A trustworthy man informed me, traced back to 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding His words: ﴿and the righteous of the believers﴾, that it is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Its chain is weak, and it is extremely unusual (munkar).

Al-Bukhari said: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: 'Umar said: "The wives of the Prophet ﷺ gathered together in jealousy over him, so I said to them: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾, and then this verse was revealed" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4916].

It has already been mentioned that he (i.e., 'Umar) agreed with the Qur'an in several places, among them the revelation regarding the veil, and among them the prisoners of Badr, and among them his saying: "Should you not take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿And take from the Station of Ibrahim a place of prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 125].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, and al-Ansari narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "News reached me of something that had passed between the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet ﷺ, so I went around questioning them (fastaqraytuhunna), saying: 'You must stop, or Allah will surely replace him with wives better than you.' Until I came to the last of the Mothers of the Believers, and she said: 'O Umar! Does the Messenger of Allah not admonish his wives, that you must admonish them?!' So I fell silent. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, submissive, faithful, obedient, penitent, worshipping, travelling, previously married and virgins﴾."

This woman who turned him back from admonishing the wives was Umm Salamah, as is established in Sahih al-Bukhari [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4483. I have not found in it an explicit statement that she was Umm Salamah, and Allah knows best].

Al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Na'ilah al-Asbahani narrated to us, Isma'il al-Bajali narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾. He said: Hafsah entered upon the Prophet ﷺ in her house while he was with Mariyah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Do not tell 'A'ishah until I give you good news: your father will govern the affair after Abu Bakr if I die." So Hafsah went and told 'A'ishah. 'A'ishah said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Who informed you of this?" He said: ﴿The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me﴾. 'A'ishah said: "I will not look at you until you forbid Mariyah," so he forbade her, and Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid...﴾ [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/117). Its weakness: in it is Isma'il al-Bajali, who is weak, and al-Dahhak did not meet Ibn Abbas, so it is disconnected (munqati').]

Its chain is open to question, and what we have cited makes clear the explanation of these noble verses. The meaning of His words ﴿Muslimat, mu'minat, qanitat, ta'ibat, 'abidat﴾ is evident.

* *

As for His words ﴿sa'ihat﴾, it means fasting women (sa'imat). This was said by Abu Hurayrah, 'A'ishah, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Malik, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, and others. A marfu' hadith about it has already been mentioned at His words ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾ in Surah al-Bara'ah, and its wording is: "The travelling of this Ummah is fasting."

Zayd ibn Aslam and his son 'Abd al-Rahman said: ﴿sa'ihat﴾ means emigrating women (muhajirat). 'Abd al-Rahman recited: ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾ [al-Tawbah: 112], meaning the emigrants (al-muhajirun). The first opinion is more preferable, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words ﴿thayyibat wa abkara﴾, it means that among them are previously married women and among them are virgins, so that this would be more appealing to souls, for variety refreshes the soul; this is why He said: ﴿thayyibat wa abkara﴾.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Abu Bakr ibn Sadaqah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Umayyah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Quddus narrated to us, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father: ﴿thayyibat wa abkara﴾. He said: Allah promised His Prophet ﷺ in this verse that He would marry him to them; the thayyib is Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh, and the abkar is Maryam daughter of 'Imran [I have not found this in the published Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani].

Mujahid said: ﴿Guard yourselves and your families against a Fire﴾, he said: "Fear Allah, and enjoin your families to have taqwa (God-consciousness) of Allah."

Qatadah said: He commands them to obey Allah and forbids them from disobeying Allah, and that he should stand over them with the command of Allah, and command them to it and help them to it. So when you see a disobedience to Allah, you should prevent them from it and restrain them from it.

This is the wording of Abu Dawud. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."

Abu Dawud also narrated, from the hadith of Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of that.

* *

The elderly man said: "O Messenger of Allah, are the stones of Hell like the stones of this world?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, a single rock from the rocks of Hell is greater than all the mountains of this world." He said: The elderly man fell unconscious, so the Prophet (ﷺ) placed his hand upon his heart, and it was still beating. He called to him: "O shaykh, say: 'There is no god but Allah.'" So he said it, and he gave him the good news of Paradise. He said: His companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, is he from among us?" He said: "Yes. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿That is for one who fears My standing and fears My threat﴾ [Ibrahim: 14]." This is a mursal, gharib hadith.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Over it are angels, harsh and severe﴾, meaning: their natures are coarse, mercy for the disbelievers in Allah has been removed from their hearts. ﴿Severe﴾ means: their construction is in the utmost severity, density and frightening appearance.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ikrimah, that he said: When the first of the people of the Fire reach the Fire, they find at the gate four hundred thousand of the guardians of Hell, their faces black, their fangs bared, Allah having removed mercy from their hearts. There is not in the heart of any one of them the weight of an atom of mercy. If a bird were flown from the shoulder of one of them, it would fly for two months before reaching his other shoulder. Then they find at the gate the nineteen, the breadth of the chest of one of them is seventy autumns. Then they plunge from gate to gate for five hundred years, and at each gate they find the same as they found at the first gate, until they reach its last.

* *

As for His words: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾, meaning: whatever He, the Exalted, commands them, they hasten to it, not delaying from it for the blink of an eye, and they are capable of doing it, there being no inability in them to do it. These are the Zabaniyah — we seek refuge with Allah from them. As for His words: ﴿O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses today; you are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾, meaning: it will be said to the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: "Make no excuses, for it will not be accepted from you, and you are only being recompensed today for your deeds."

Al-Thawri said, from Simak, from al-Nu'man, from Umar: "Sincere repentance is that one repents from the sin and then does not return to it, or does not return to it."

Abu al-Ahwas and others said, from Simak, from al-Nu'man: Umar was asked about sincere repentance, and he said: "That a man repents from the evil deed and then never returns to it."

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah: ﴿Sincere repentance﴾ — he said: "He repents and then does not return."

This has also been narrated as a marfu' report. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, from Ibrahim al-Hajari, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Repentance from a sin is that one repents from it and then does not return to it." ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed You are over all things competent."﴾ Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan al-Basri and others said: This is what the believers will say on the Day of Resurrection when they see the light of the hypocrites has been extinguished.

Ibn Nasr al-Marwazi said: Muhammad ibn Muqatil al-Marwazi narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah informed us: Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, that he heard Abu Dharr and Abu al-Darda say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will be the first to be permitted to prostrate on the Day of Resurrection, and the first to be permitted to raise his head. I will look in front of me and recognize my Ummah among the nations; I will look to my right and recognize my Ummah among the nations; I will look to my left and recognize my Ummah among the nations." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize your Ummah among the nations?" He said: "They will be bright-faced and white-limbed from the traces of ablution (wudu'), and no one else among the nations will be like that. Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hassan, from a man of the Banu Kinanah who said: "I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the year of the Conquest, and I heard him saying: 'O Allah, do not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection.'"

I will look in front of me and recognize my Ummah among the nations; I will look to my right and recognize my Ummah among the nations; I will look to my left and recognize my Ummah among the nations." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize your Ummah among the nations?" He said: "They will be bright-faced and white-limbed from the traces of ablution (wudu'), and no one else among the nations will be like that. I will recognize them because they will be given their records in their right hands, and I will recognize them by their marks on their faces from the trace of prostration, and I will recognize them by their light running before them."

[Ta'zim Qadr al-Salah (Magnifying the Status of Prayer), no. 261. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (5/199) by this route, the route of Ibn al-Mubarak, and through Hasan, from Ibn Lahi'ah, with similar wording. Al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/151): "Ahmad narrated it, and in its chain is Ibn Lahi'ah, and it is a hadith used in corroborative narrations (mutaba'at)."
