Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hassan, from a man of the Banu Kinanah who said: "I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the year of the Conquest, and I heard him saying: 'O Allah, do not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection.'"

[Al-Musnad (4/234)]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 66, verse 6–8 (part 1 of 2):

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from a man, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning His words, ﴿Guard yourselves and your families against a Fire﴾, that he said: "Discipline them and teach them."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Guard yourselves and your families against a Fire﴾ means: "Act in obedience to Allah, and guard against the disobedience of Allah, and command your families to remember Allah, and Allah will save you from the Fire."

Mujahid said: ﴿Guard yourselves and your families against a Fire﴾, he said: "Fear Allah, and enjoin your families to have taqwa (God-consciousness) of Allah."

Qatadah said: He commands them to obey Allah and forbids them from disobeying Allah, and that he should stand over them with the command of Allah, and command them to it and help them to it. So when you see a disobedience to Allah, you should prevent them from it and restrain them from it.

Likewise al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: It is incumbent upon the Muslim to teach his family, including his relatives, his female slaves and his male slaves, what Allah has made obligatory upon them and what Allah has forbidden them.

In the meaning of this verse is the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn al-Rabi ibn Sabrah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Command your children to pray when they reach seven years of age, and when they reach ten years of age, strike them for it."

This is the wording of Abu Dawud. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."

Abu Dawud also narrated, from the hadith of Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of that.

The jurists said: Likewise regarding fasting, so that it is a training for him in worship, so that he reaches adulthood while being steadfast in worship, obedience, keeping away from disobedience and abandoning what is evil. And Allah is the Granter of success.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Its fuel is people and stones﴾. ﴿Its fuel﴾ means its firewood, which is the bodies of the children of Adam that are thrown into it. ﴿And stones﴾ — it has been said that what is meant by this is the idols that were worshipped, based on His words: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98].

Ibn Mas'ud, Mujahid, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir and al-Suddi said: They are stones of sulphur. Mujahid added: "More foul-smelling than carrion."

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated this, then said: My father narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sinan al-Minqari narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz — meaning Ibn Abi Rawwad — narrated to us, saying: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, guard yourselves and your families against a Fire whose fuel is people and stones﴾, while some of his companions were with him, and among them was an elderly man. The elderly man said: "O Messenger of Allah, are the stones of Hell like the stones of this world?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, a single rock from the rocks of Hell is greater than all the mountains of this world." He said: The elderly man fell unconscious, so the Prophet (ﷺ) placed his hand upon his heart, and it was still beating. He called to him: "O shaykh, say: 'There is no god but Allah.'" So he said it, and he gave him the good news of Paradise. He said: His companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, is he from among us?" He said: "Yes. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿That is for one who fears My standing and fears My threat﴾ [Ibrahim: 14]." This is a mursal, gharib hadith.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Over it are angels, harsh and severe﴾, meaning: their natures are coarse, mercy for the disbelievers in Allah has been removed from their hearts. ﴿Severe﴾ means: their construction is in the utmost severity, density and frightening appearance.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ikrimah, that he said: When the first of the people of the Fire reach the Fire, they find at the gate four hundred thousand of the guardians of Hell, their faces black, their fangs bared, Allah having removed mercy from their hearts. There is not in the heart of any one of them the weight of an atom of mercy. If a bird were flown from the shoulder of one of them, it would fly for two months before reaching his other shoulder. Then they find at the gate the nineteen, the breadth of the chest of one of them is seventy autumns. Then they plunge from gate to gate for five hundred years, and at each gate they find the same as they found at the first gate, until they reach its last.

* *

As for His words: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾, meaning: whatever He, the Exalted, commands them, they hasten to it, not delaying from it for the blink of an eye, and they are capable of doing it, there being no inability in them to do it. These are the Zabaniyah — we seek refuge with Allah from them. As for His words: ﴿O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses today; you are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾, meaning: it will be said to the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: "Make no excuses, for it will not be accepted from you, and you are only being recompensed today for your deeds."

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance﴾, meaning: a truthful, resolute repentance, which erases the evil deeds before it and gathers the scattered affairs of the repentant and restrains him from the baseness he used to engage in.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb: I heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir giving a sermon: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, say concerning ﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance﴾: "It is that one commits a sin and then does not return to it."

Al-Thawri said, from Simak, from al-Nu'man, from Umar: "Sincere repentance is that one repents from the sin and then does not return to it, or does not return to it."

Abu al-Ahwas and others said, from Simak, from al-Nu'man: Umar was asked about sincere repentance, and he said: "That a man repents from the evil deed and then never returns to it."

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah: ﴿Sincere repentance﴾ — he said: "He repents and then does not return."

This has also been narrated as a marfu' report. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, from Ibrahim al-Hajari, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Repentance from a sin is that one repents from it and then does not return to it." Ahmad alone narrated it through the route of Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, and he is weak, and the mawquf report is more authentic. And Allah knows best.

For this reason the scholars said: Sincere repentance is that one desists from the sin in the present, regrets what preceded from it in the past, and resolves not to do it in the future. Then, if the right involved is that of a human being, he returns it to him by its proper means.

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim, Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam informed me, from Abd Allah ibn Ma'qil, who said: I entered with my father upon Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and he said: "Did you hear the Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'Regret is repentance'?" He said: "Yes." And at another time he said: "Yes, I heard him say: 'Regret is repentance.'"

Ibn Majah narrated it from Hisham ibn Ammar, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Abd al-Karim — that is Ibn Malik al-Jazari — with the same chain. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "This is a sahih chain, all of its narrators are trustworthy."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Arafah narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Bukayr Abu Khabbab narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Adawi, from Abu Sinan al-Basri, from Abu Qilabah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "We were told of things that will occur at the end of this Ummah as the Hour draws near. Among them: a man having intercourse with his wife or his female slave in her rear, and that is among what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and Allah and His Messenger abhor it. Among them: a man marrying a man, and that is among what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and Allah and His Messenger abhor it. Among them: a woman marrying a woman, and that is among what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and Allah and His Messenger abhor it. And these people have no prayer so long as they persist in this, until they repent to Allah with sincere repentance." Zirr said: "I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: 'What is sincere repentance?' He said: 'I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "It is regret for the sin when it escapes from you, so that you seek forgiveness of Allah through your regret for it in the present, and then you never return to it."'" [Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Shu'ab al-Iman from the route of Isma'il al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Arafah, and said: "Its chain is weak."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, Abbad ibn Amr narrated to us, Abu Amr ibn al-Ala narrated to us: I heard al-Hasan say: "Sincere repentance is that you hate the sin as you once loved it, and seek forgiveness from it whenever you remember it."

As for one who resolves upon repentance and firmly determines upon it, then it erases what preceded it of wrongs, as is established in the Sahih: "Islam erases what came before it, and repentance erases what came before it." [Sahih Muslim, no. 121, from the hadith of Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Is it a condition of sincere repentance that one persists in it until death, as has preceded in the hadith and the report: "he does not return to it ever"? Or is the resolve not to return sufficient for the expiation of the past, such that if that sin occurs from him afterwards, it does not harm the expiation of what preceded? This is based on the generality of his words, peace be upon him: "Repentance erases what came before it." The first position may argue from what is also established in the Sahih: "Whoever does good in Islam will not be held accountable for what he did in the Jahiliyyah, and whoever does evil in Islam will be held accountable for the first and the last." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6921, and Sahih Muslim, no. 120, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.] So if this is the case in Islam, which is stronger than repentance, then repentance is more so. And Allah knows best.

As for His words: ﴿It may be that your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. The "it may be" (asa) from Allah is binding. ﴿On the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him﴾, meaning: and He will not disgrace them along with him, on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Their light will run before them and on their right﴾, as has preceded in Surat al-Hadid.

﴿They will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed You are over all things competent."﴾ Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan al-Basri and others said: This is what the believers will say on the Day of Resurrection when they see the light of the hypocrites has been extinguished.

Ibn Nasr al-Marwazi said: Muhammad ibn Muqatil al-Marwazi narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah informed us: Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, that he heard Abu Dharr and Abu al-Darda say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will be the first to be permitted to prostrate on the Day of Resurrection, and the first to be permitted to raise his head. I will look in front of me and recognize my Ummah among the nations; I will look to my right and recognize my Ummah among the nations; I will look to my left and recognize my Ummah among the nations." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize your Ummah among the nations?" He said: "They will be bright-faced and white-limbed from the traces of ablution (wudu'), and no one else among the nations will be like that. I will recognize them because they will be given their records in their right hands, and I will recognize them by their marks on their faces from the trace of prostration, and I will recognize them by their light running before them."

[Ta'zim Qadr al-Salah (Magnifying the Status of Prayer), no. 261. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (5/199) by this route, the route of Ibn al-Mubarak, and through Hasan, from Ibn Lahi'ah, with similar wording. Al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/151): "Ahmad narrated it, and in its chain is Ibn Lahi'ah, and it is a hadith used in corroborative narrations (mutaba'at)." Here it is narrated through Ibn al-Mubarak, and that narration is sound.]

Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hassan, from a man of the Banu Kinanah who said: "I prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the year of the Conquest, and I heard him saying: 'O Allah, do not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection.'"

[Al-Musnad (4/234)]

The Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 66, verses 9–10:

God, exalted is He, says, commanding His Messenger ﷺ to strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites: the former with weapons and fighting, and the latter by enforcing the hudud (the prescribed punishments) upon them. ﴿And be harsh with them﴾, meaning in this world, ﴿and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾, meaning in the Hereafter. [[In manuscript M: "in the other one" (fi al-ukhra).]]

Then He said: ﴿God presents an example for those who disbelieve﴾, meaning through their close association with the believers and their living among them, that this does not benefit them at all, nor does it avail them with God, if faith has not taken root in their hearts. Then He mentioned the example, saying: ﴿the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants﴾, meaning two prophets and messengers, ﴿and they betrayed them﴾, who were with them in their company by night and by day, eating with them, sleeping with them, and living with them in the closest companionship and mixing. [[In manuscript M: "in their company, both of them."]] ﴿They betrayed them﴾, meaning in faith: they did not agree with them in faith, nor did they confirm them in the message. So none of that availed them anything, nor did it ward off any harm from them. Therefore He said: ﴿so they availed them nothing against God﴾, meaning because of their disbelief, ﴿and it was said﴾, meaning to the two women: ﴿Enter the Fire with those who enter﴾.

The intended meaning of ﴿they betrayed them﴾ is not betrayal in immorality, but in religion, for the wives of the prophets are protected from falling into immorality, out of respect for the prophets, as we have mentioned in Surah al-Nur.

Sufyan al-Thawri reported from Musa ibn Abi 'A'isha, from Sulayman ibn Qatta, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say concerning this verse, ﴿they betrayed them﴾: "They did not commit adultery. As for the wife of Noah, she used to tell people that he was a madman. As for the betrayal of the wife of Lot, she used to point her people to his guests."

Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Their betrayal was that they were against them in their private matters. The wife of Noah would learn the secret of Noah, and whenever anyone believed with Noah, she would inform the tyrants of Noah's people about him. As for the wife of Lot, whenever Lot hosted anyone, she would inform the people of the city of him, among those who did evil."

Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and others said the same.

[Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "The wife of no prophet ever committed adultery; their betrayal was only in religion."] [[Addition from manuscript M.]]

Some scholars have used this noble verse to argue against the weakness of the hadith that many people narrate: "Whoever eats with one who has been forgiven, he will be forgiven." This hadith has no basis. It is narrated only from some of the righteous, who said that they saw the Prophet ﷺ in a dream and said: "O Messenger of God, did you say, 'Whoever eats with one who has been forgiven, he will be forgiven'?" He said: "No, but I am now saying it." [[Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: "This has no chain of narration (isnad) according to the scholars, nor is it found in any of the books of the Muslims. They only narrate it from Sinan, and its meaning is not correct in absolute terms, for a disbeliever and a hypocrite may eat with Muslims." Quoted by al-Albani in al-Silsilah al-Da'ifah (1/326). Imam Ibn al-Qayyim mentioned it in al-Manar al-Munif (p. 140) and said: "It is fabricated (mawdu'), and the most that is reported about it is that it was a dream seen by some people."]]

This is an example Allah sets for the believers: that mixing with disbelievers does not harm them when they are not dependent on them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers. Whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah, except when you fear a danger from them.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 28].

Qatadah said: "Pharaoh was the most arrogant and remote of the people of the earth, yet by Allah, the disbelief of her husband did not harm his wife when she obeyed her Lord, so that you may know that Allah is a just Judge who does not punish anyone except for his own sin."

Ibn Jarir said: Isma'il ibn Hafs al-Ubulli narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi [[In A: "al-Tirmidhi".]], from Salman, who said: "The wife of Pharaoh was tortured in the sun. When he left her, the angels would shade her with their wings, and she would see her house in Paradise."

He then narrated it from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi, from Asbat ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman al-Taymi, with the same wording. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/110).]]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastuwa'i, Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah narrated to us, who said: "The wife of Pharaoh used to ask: 'Who has won?' It would be said: 'Musa and Harun have won.' She would say: 'I believe in the Lord of Musa and Harun.' Pharaoh sent for her, and she said: 'Look for the largest rock you can find. If she persists in her statement, throw it on her; and if she retracts her statement, she is his wife.' When they came to her, she raised her eyes to the sky and saw her house in Paradise. She persisted in her statement, her soul was taken, and the rock was thrown onto a body with no soul in it." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/110).]]

As for her words: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾, the scholars said: "She chose the neighbour before the house." Something of this has been reported in a raised (marfu') hadith. ﴿And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾, meaning: rescue me from him, for I disown his deeds. ﴿And save me from the wrongdoing people﴾. This woman was Asiyah bint Muzahim, may Allah be pleased with her.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: "The faith of the wife of Pharaoh came before the faith of the wife of Pharaoh's treasurer. She was sitting and combing the hair of Pharaoh's daughter, when the comb fell from her hand. She said: 'Perish the one who disbelieves in Allah!' Pharaoh's daughter said to her: 'Do you have a lord other than my father?' She said: 'My Lord, your Lord, and the Lord of everything is Allah.' Pharaoh's daughter slapped her and struck her, and told her father. Pharaoh sent for her and said: 'Do you worship a lord other than me?' She said: 'Yes, my Lord, your Lord, and the Lord of everything is Allah, and Him alone I worship.' So Pharaoh tortured her, drove stakes for her, bound her hands and feet, and set snakes upon her. She remained in this state. One day he came to her and said: 'Will you not desist?' She said: 'My Lord, your Lord, and the Lord of everything is Allah.' He said: 'I will slaughter your son in front of you if you do not do so.' She said: 'Do what you will decide.' So he slaughtered her son before her face, and the soul of her son gave her good news, saying: 'Rejoice, O mother, for you have such-and-such reward with Allah.' She remained patient. Then Pharaoh came to her another day and said to her the same thing, and she answered him the same way. He slaughtered her other son before her face, and his soul also gave her good news and said to her: 'Be patient, O mother, for you have such-and-such reward with Allah.'" He said: "The wife of Pharaoh heard the speech of the souls of her elder son and then her younger son. So the wife of Pharaoh believed. Allah took the soul of Pharaoh's treasurer's wife, and He uncovered for the wife of Pharaoh the veil over her reward, her station and her honour in Paradise, until she saw it, and her faith, certainty and affirmation increased. Pharaoh became aware of her faith, and said to the chiefs: 'What do you know of Asiyah bint Muzahim?' They praised her. He said to them: 'She worships other than me.' They said to him: 'Kill her.' So he drove stakes for her and bound her hands and feet. Asiyah called upon her Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾. It so happened that when Pharaoh was present, she laughed when she saw her house in Paradise. Pharaoh said: 'Do you not wonder at her madness? We torture her and she laughs!' Then Allah took her soul, may Allah be pleased with her." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (28/10).]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity﴾, meaning she preserved and protected it. Ihsan (chastity) means purity and freedom from unlawful acts. ﴿So We breathed into it of Our Spirit﴾, meaning through an angel, who is Jibril (Gabriel). Allah sent him to her, and he appeared to her in the form of a perfectly formed human. Allah commanded him to blow with his mouth into the opening of her garment.
